what_this_is: Crystal E4 deliverable R0 (reports/crystal-lane/2026-09-24-remaining-plan/items.json, entry e4-relations): every deployed reduction / conversion / inference family reachable from the release TypeChecker::infer_type, keyed to clean-kernel source, mapped to exactly one of covered (a constructor or registered declaration of the env-indexed target family), excluded (a named precondition), or MISSING. Read-only: nothing here changes the spec or the kernel. Ratchet: scripts/crystal_e4_inventory.py re-derives the function census, the site sets, the target constructor sets and every citation from source, every run.
plan_alignment: This is the first slice of the 'explicit coverage inventory for every acceptance path' that plan Milestone 5 calls for (docs/plans/SELF_VERIFICATION_RUST_LEAN_PLAN_2026-09-22.md, commit 04371854d); no artifact with that purpose existed in the tree (checked 2026-09-24: the plan and the execution ledger name it, the ledger's 'bounded inventory' is a call census of the literal helper). Scope of THIS slice: the conversion / inference / reduction families under infer_type. Declaration admission (Milestone 3) and the Trust-contract lane's Literal / BigNat / Arc<str> / Name representation (b8264b871, e42b4ed81, 0f2c08b62) are not rows here; the representation obligations they own are named in row notes (R4) rather than duplicated. Milestone 5 should extend THIS file rather than mint another.

classes.covered: a named constructor (or registered declaration) of DefEqIn / DefEqCDPIn / KernelInfersIn / TypingCtxConvIn, or of their successors KernelAcceptsIn / TypingCDPCtxConvIn / TypingProjIn and the typed-conversion KernelAcceptsTcIn / TypingTcIn carries the family; 'via' cites the sub-relation constructor or definition that does the work. Covered is a statement about the RELATION; each note names the implementation/representation obligation still open.
classes.excluded: outside the proved fragment by a named precondition: configuration (a represented state can pin it), obligation (stated, NOT discharged), or scope (not reached from infer_type).
classes.MISSING: no constructor of the target family carries it; spec cites the relation it is absent from, evidence cites where the tree already records the gap.
classes.path: Every row that was MISSING at 2026-09-24 carries `path`: whether the deployed infer_type path the link-4 proof is about TAKES the branch (taken), why, and its rank (1 = closest to infer_type's own frame / most often taken). A MISSING row must be taken (a branch the path does not take is `excluded` with its reason); ranks are unique. The checker enforces both.

precondition_answer.question: Memo D5(b)/§5: is the declarative target 'KernelInfers' closed under the deployed delta/iota reductions?
precondition_answer.answer: NO -- and the question was mis-posed: KernelInfers is ALGORITHMIC and pinned to the_red_env.
findings: KernelInfers is the algorithmic relation (dependent_sn_richmodel.rs, `inductive KernelInfers`), and its conversion DefEq reduces through delta_reduces / iota_reduces, each of whose sole constructor is pinned to `the_red_env` (typing_def_eq_reduction_families.rs): it cannot represent any deployed environment.

The deployed iota whnf-reduces the MAJOR (with delta) before rule lookup; the reflected iota_reduct does not (iota_prepass.rs). Even the env-indexed KernelInfersIn's whnf premise (whnf_red_step) has head iota only on a constructor-headed major.

Smart imax: the deployed Pi arm returns Sort(self.level_imax(l1, l2)): under Extended the smart constructor Level::imax (level/mod.rs), under Lean/LeanReference Lean's mk_imax (R150), while KernelInfers and ImplInfer return raw Level.imax, so Pi(Sort 0, Sort 0) is Sort 1 deployed and Sort (imax 1 1) in the model. KernelInfersIn.pi accepts it through levelEqSem.

Default state: every TypeChecker constructor sets infer_only = Cell::new(true) (tc/config.rs), under which the release App/Lam/Let arms skip their checks; a soundness conjunct over every represented input is false unless infer_only = false is pinned.
The right target is the env-indexed family DefEqIn / DefEqCDPIn / TypingCtxConvIn / KernelInfersIn (acceptance_in.rs, with kernel_infers_in_sound); this inventory maps the deployed families onto it.

Extended target (Crystal E4 increments): KernelAcceptsIn (acceptance_cdp_in/inference.rs), the algorithmic successor of KernelInfersIn, takes every whnf premise as par_reduces_cdp_star -- which carries the major pre-pass and proj-iota -- and every conversion premise as DefEqCDPIn, adds the Proj inference arm, and is sound into TypingProjIn (TypingCDPCtxConvIn plus the projection rule) by kernel_accepts_in_sound. The families par_reduces_cdp does not carry stay MISSING (infer-whnf-premise-residual and the conv-* rows).

rows.family: structure-eta expansion of a non-constructor major (try_eta_struct)
rows.note: A reduction step inside whnf, carried as CONVERSION: KernelAcceptsTcIn's whnf premises are conversions of the same family, so the step major == expand_eta_struct(type, major) is struct_eta with t := the expansion, whose field premises are refl (field i IS proj i major); iota on the constructor-headed major is DefEqCDPIn. The witness's t is exactly the expansion of #0 at the one-field structure. The Prop guard (Guard 4) only narrows; since R147 (leanprover/lean4#14843) it asks is_prop, which errs unless the type's type whnfs to a sort, and an error leaves the major as it is. Premises are CHECK-mode derivations of the subjects; the deployed branch infers them in infer-only mode (try_infer_type_quick / infer_type_infer_only), and that the two agree on the subjects that reach is_def_eq is the infer_only_conditional obligation, NOT DISCHARGED.

rows.family: K-like reduction (try_to_cnstr_when_k)
rows.note: items.json R2(f); typed. Covered (E4d, 2026-09-28): one rule per family, KernelAcceptsTcIn.k_like / TypingTcIn.k_like, keyed on RecKAdmitIn R rn I mta cn -- the admission fact as a SYNTACTIC predicate over R (the vacuity firewall forbids a KernelAcceptsTcIn arm to mention TypingTcIn): recmeta_for rn = mta with recmeta_k_flag mta = 1, exactly one rule, for cn with no fields, cn's parent I non-mutual with cn its only constructor and I's type ending in Sort 0 -- what clean main 67288ad33's regenerated recursors guarantee of rec_val.is_k. RecMeta gained the K flag as a Nat field (a Bool field would renumber interning tags 6/7 that hand-written spec text cites); the red-env reflector emits the kernel's is_k there, so the reflected seed's Eq.rec carries flag 1 and is admitted (accepts_k_eq_rec_admitted). The arm mirrors try_to_cnstr_when_k: the major's type M whnfs to W (a conversion premise), W's head is I, the constructor application is cn applied to W's first num_params arguments, its type C is inferred and W == C; conclusion major == ctor app, which the recursor spine carries by app_cong before ordinary iota (accepts_k_iota_witness: a recursor applied to the HYPOTHESIS #0 reduces to its minor). Soundness is one arm of kernel_accepts_tc_in_sound. Justification, stated not assumed: typing_tc_in_k_like_is_proof_irrel derives every TypingTcIn.k_like instance from proof_irrel once W is typed at a sort converting to Sort 0 -- a regularity fact the admission gives for a well-typed major but the deployed step never checks, so it is an obligation of the target's k_like rule, not a premise. Three forged callers are refused (flag 0, an inductive in Type, a constructor with a field).

path.why: try_iota_reduction's K conversion whenever rec_val.is_k (Eq.rec / Eq.ndrec and every K-like recursor); taken by every cast / rewrite over an equation proof that is not Eq.refl.

rows.family: Quot.lift / Quot.ind reduction
rows.note: items.json R2(f). Covered (E4c, 2026-09-27): Lean 4's quot_reduce_rec as one rule per eliminator in both families, KernelAcceptsTcIn.quot_lift / quot_ind and TypingTcIn.quot_lift / quot_ind: Quot.lift A r B f h (Quot.mk A2 r2 a) == f a and Quot.ind A r B f (Quot.mk A2 r2 a) == f a, keyed on the reflected Quot.lift / Quot.ind / Quot.mk (reserved native rule keys of the red-env generator, red_env_reflect::RESERVED_NATIVE_RULE_KEYS, appended at tags 165-167 without renumbering; every key must name a prelude constant). No environment gate on either side, as deployed. The deployed whnf of the major and the trailing arguments are conversions carried by app_cong; soundness is one arm of kernel_accepts_tc_in_sound. Witnessed at every environment: a lift whose major is a beta-redex, a plain ind redex, and a lift under a trailing argument; three forged callers refused (a two-argument Quot.mk, an ind head through the lift rule, the proof argument returned). Divergence, found by reading, not a finding: the deployed try_quot_lift_reduction / try_quot_ind_reduction accept a Quot.mk major with MORE than three arguments (major_args.len() < 3 declines) and take args[2], where Lean requires exactly three; the rules here require three, so an ill-typed over-applied Quot.mk major (Quot r is not a Pi, so a well-typed major never has four) is the only deployed acceptance they do not carry.

path.why: beta_or_iota_step's try_quot_reduction, keyed on the Quot.lift / Quot.ind names (no environment gate); taken for quotient eliminators applied to Quot.mk.

rows.family: native Nat literal arithmetic (reduce_nat; eager_reduce widens it to open terms)
rows.note: items.json R2(e): one lemma per operation. Covered (E4d, 2026-09-28) by DERIVED lemmas, no new arm: since clean main df9163459 each reduce_nat fold fires only when the head's delta-closure digest is pinned (env/native_fold_canon.tsv), and for every key the specification world admits a lemma PROVES, over any R holding the canonical closure (and Nat.rec's canonical rules), op (literal a) (literal b) == literal (op a b) by delta / beta / iota (KernelAcceptsTcIn.cdp) and lit_zero / lit_succ alone -- one induction mirroring the definition, the meta-level op on the right being the same definition, empty axiom closure (census acceptance_cdp_in_census). The canonical bodies are reflected from the LIVE environment at registration and the proofs re-checked against them (acceptance_cdp_in/native_nat.rs; minted by scripts/gen_accepts_tc_native_nat.py). Keys and lemmas: succ (the literal rule), pred, add, sub, mul, pow, shiftLeft, beq, ble, div, mod (fuel-bounded divCore / modCore), land / lor / xor (Nat.bitwise over div2 / testBit, with Prod projections by projection-beta and Bool.rec) and shiftRight (registered LATE: the build defines Nat.shiftRight at its end), each with a witness instance and its TypingTcIn corollary through kernel_accepts_tc_in_sound. The deployed fold whnfs each operand to a literal first; that step is an ordinary derivation composed by app_cong / trans. The E4c findings are closed by the kernel gate, not here: Nat.gcd folds only where its digest is pinned, and a value-less axiom head such as with_prelude's Nat.shiftRight gets the verdict HeadNotDefinition (read in env/native_fold_authority.rs; measured for the axioms Int.div / Int.mod in the specification world), so no fold fires on it. RESIDUAL, stated: (1) Nat.gcd, the sixteenth key, is absent from the specification world (pinned only for lean-v4.30.0-rc2), so no lemma is claimed for it; (2) the other pinned worlds' bodies (Clean's own prelude where it differs, Lean's Init) each need their own agreement lemma over their own body; (3) not extracted Rust execution -- the lemma carries the fold's RESULT, and BigNat arithmetic agreeing with the definition is the fold table's pin, not proved here.

path.why: whnf_core_inner's App arm tries reduce_nat BEFORE unfolding a Nat.* head and whnf_outer_loop tries it after every delta step; any closed Nat arithmetic in a type takes it. Gated only on the head names and literal arguments.

rows.family: registered native reducers (Lean.reduceBool/Nat, decide, UInt ofNat argument normalisation, BitVec, wrapper comparisons)
rows.note: items.json R2(e). registry_reducer_admitted (tc/fold_admission.rs) requires the kernel theory to admit the head AND fold_admitted (a pinned closure digest in env/native_fold_canon.tsv) AND every recognized-argument name to be canonical, so a registered reducer fires only on a head whose closure digest is pinned. MEASURED (E4n, 2026-09-29, over the full Specification via native_fold_verdict, every registered_native_reducer_name plus the reduce_nat/reduce_int keys): 60 registered heads are admitted. E4d's derived lemmas carry 22 (Nat.pred/add/sub/mul/div/mod/pow/beq/ble/land/lor/xor/shiftLeft/shiftRight, Int.add/sub/mul/neg, Bool.not/and/or/xor). E4n adds 2 more DERIVED agreement lemmas, quantified over any R holding the canonical closure, kernel-checked with EMPTY domain and foundational axiom closures (accepts_tc_native_fold_census, generated/accepts_tc_native_nat.json): kernel_accepts_tc_in_nat_blt_fold (Nat.blt a b delta-unfolds to Nat.ble (Nat.succ a) b, closed by the proven Nat.ble fold at (succ a, b)) and kernel_accepts_tc_in_int_tonat_fold (Int.toNat delta+Int.rec-iota to the payload Nat literal on Int.ofNat, to Nat.zero on Int.negSucc). 36 remain, in four measured groups. (1) DERIVABLE, not yet built -- the fold is definitional over the environment (delta/iota to a literal, or an unfolding to the same Decidable.isX constructor whose proof field is bridged by proof irrelevance), a per-head induction like the E4d folds, the next E4n increment: List.length, Bool.beq, Int.ble, BEq.beq (delta to the instance's beq), decide, Decidable.decide, Nat.decEq, Nat.decLe, Nat.decLt, Bool.decEq, Int.decEq, instDecidableAnd, instDecidableNot, instDecidableOr, instDecidableNatLe, instDecidableNatLt, instDecidableEqBool, instDecidableEqInt, instDecidableEqNat. (2) PAYLOAD -- the deployed reducer computes over the bare-Nat-literal PAYLOAD representation of a Fin/BitVec/UInt/Char value; a bare literal is not a model term at that carrier, so the intermediate steps have no KExpr image. The full-constructor iota chain (Fin.mk / BitVec.ofFin / Char.mk) is derivable, but the deployed reducer takes the payload shortcut -- reported as a SOUNDNESS question (the model justifies only the full-constructor equivalent, not the shortcut): Fin.val, BitVec.toNat, BitVec.toFin, UInt32.toNat, UInt32.toBitVec, Char.toNat, and the decEqs whose isFalse witness projects through them -- Char.decEq, instDecidableEqChar, UInt32.decEq, instDecidableEqUInt32, instDecidableEqFin. (3) STRING -- derivable since E4 String (the literal expansion is the model rule KernelAcceptsTcIn.lit_string_expand, conv-string-literal-expansion), not yet built: each fold is lit_string_expand on the operand literals followed by the delta / iota unfolding of String.length / String.beq / String.decEq over the expanded List Char (the Decidable ones bridged by proof irrelevance as in (1)), under StringLitAdmitIn and valid characters; in the Lean 4.30 world the payload is UTF-8 bytes, so each world needs its own lemma: String.beq, String.decEq, String.length, instDecidableEqString. The phase-7 step is_def_eq(whnf(expansion), s) is the derived accepts_tc_string_lit_expansion (the rule, then the whnf conversion, then the comparison, by trans); accepts_tc_lit_string_every_payload covers EVERY payload (the decoding is onto). Soundness is one arm of kernel_accepts_tc_in_sound. Witness at the canonical-closure fixture accepts_tc_string_env: "ab" to its expansion and on to String.mk [..] by delta / beta; near misses (a wrong character, a wrong length, the String.mk head in place of String.ofList, a surrogate, a swapped order, the seed's tables, an identity String.ofList) refused. REPRESENTATION, discharged: the payload of literal_string IS the character list (literal_string_codec: string_lit_code / string_lit_chars, a bijection proved both ways, string_lit_code_chars and string_lit_chars_code, empty axiom closure), so a deployed Literal::String(s) is literal_string (string_lit_code cs) for cs = s.chars() as scalar values -- the interning premise R4 named is gone; the red-env reflector renders literal leaves through the same codec (render_literal). WORLDS, measured 2026-09-29. The deployed expansion fires only under string_literal_admitted (Nat canonical and String.ofList / Char.ofNat canonical by delta-closure digest, tc/fold_admission.rs). (1) clean-prelude (Environment::with_prelude, the default --prelude builtin): both heads pinned; String is the List Char structure (String.mk the constructor) and String.ofList := fun d => String.mk d, so whnf(expansion) is String.mk [Char.ofNat c, ...]; measured on the deployed kernel: "ab" == String.ofList [97,98] and == String.mk [97,98] accepted, a wrong character / length refused, Proj(String, 0, "ab") whnfs to the Char.ofNat list. THIS is the world the model's admission fact StringLitAdmitIn pins (records reflected from with_prelude at registration, which refuses registration if the pin table stops admitting them). (2) The specification's own world: String.ofList is pinned (clean-prelude digest) but Char.ofNat is ABSENT from the specification environment, so the deployed kernel never expands a string literal there (measured: "ab" == String.ofList [..] refused, Proj(String, 0, "ab") stuck); String.rec on a literal still reduces there, by structure eta on the major (a different row). (3) Lean 4.30.0-rc2 (pinned toolchain, measured with Lean.Kernel.whnf / isDefEq): String is the ByteArray structure (String.ofByteArray); the kernel expands a literal to String.ofList [Char.ofNat c, ...] (a discriminating environment where String.ofList and String.mk build different constructors: iota on a literal major takes String.ofList's body) and whnfs it to String.ofByteArray (List.utf8Encode ..) _, so Proj 0 is the UTF-8 ByteArray and String.rec's minor sees bytes ("\u00e9" has size 2). Clean's pin table admits this world too (lean-v4.30.0-rc2 digests), but its bodies differ from clean-prelude's: an environment in it expands deployed and is NOT covered by StringLitAdmitIn's one constructor -- it needs its own admission constructor over Lean 4.30's records. (4) Lean 4.8.0 (pinned toolchain, measured): String is the List Char structure and the kernel expands to the CONSTRUCTOR String.mk [Char.ofNat c, ...] (Proj(String, 0, "ab") = List.cons.{0} Char (Char.ofNat 97) ..); String.ofList does not exist there, so the deployed kernel (keyed on String.ofList) never expands in a Lean 4.8 environment -- a completeness gap in the safe direction. (5) The def-eq trigger differs, measured in discriminating environments built from empty: Lean 4.8 expands a literal against a String.mk-headed side (a two-constructor String whose first constructor is String.mk accepts "ab" == String.mk [..]) and does not whnf the expansion (with String.mk a definition, a literal major or projection subject stays stuck); Lean 4.30 accepts no such side (the same two-constructor environment refuses it, as it refuses String.ofList- and String.ofByteArray-headed sides), and accepts "ab" == String.mk [..] only when String has one constructor, i.e. through structure eta projecting the literal. The deployed kernel expands against ANY constant-headed application (try_string_lit_expansion_core): strictly more complete than either, over the same expansion. ADMISSION RESIDUAL, stated: the deployed digest pins String.ofList's and Char.ofNat's whole delta-closures; StringLitAdmitIn pins String.ofList's record, the String.mk constructor entry and Char.ofNat's record, but not the List / Char inductive shapes String.ofList's digest also covers, nor Char.ofNat's deeper closure (86 constants reached from its value in with_prelude: Char.ofNatAux, dite, the Decidable / Or / And machinery, BitVec.ofNatLT, UInt32.ofBitVec, Char.mk, ...). So a KernelAcceptsTcIn instance can exist in an R whose deeper Char.ofNat closure is not canonical, where the deployed kernel refuses -- an over-approximation of deployed acceptance, the direction link 4 tolerates. RANGE: the rule also requires string_lit_chars_valid cs (every character a Unicode scalar value, Nat.isValidChar); a Rust str holds only those, so every deployed literal satisfies it, and without it the target would identify distinct payloads through Char.ofNat's clamp of invalid code points to 0.
